claims.text: The last 500 years contain thirteen paradigm-level replacements — not refinements but wholesale demolitions of what the previous generation called settled truth.
claims.reviewer_notes: Central factual claim of the chapter; supported by enumerated examples. Verify count and examples.

claims.text: The pessimistic meta-induction — since every successful theory of the past was eventually proven wrong, we have no inductive grounds to believe our current models are the final truth.
claims.reviewer_notes: Core philosophical argument attributed to Laudan; well-defined but requires source verification.

claims.text: Science's relationship to truth is negative rather than positive — it produces models that have not yet been shown to be false, not proven descriptions of reality.
claims.reviewer_notes: Supported by quotes from Popper, Kuhn, Bohr, Feynman, Hawking; check accuracy of attributions.

claims.text: The convergence pattern — each replacement is more accurate, more unifying, more elegant — is itself evidence that reality is coherent enough to be approached by rational minds, which is exactly what you'd expect if someone rational built it.
claims.reviewer_notes: Interpretive claim linking convergence to theism; plausible but not directly evidenced in the source.

claims.text: Every one of these presuppositions is an act of faith. And every one of them makes sense — immediately, obviously, naturally — if there's a rational mind behind reality who designed the knower to match the known.
claims.reviewer_notes: Overreached: equates presuppositions with faith without addressing naturalist alternatives; strong rhetorical claim needing nuance.
